Observed at +10.701830863952637s — page 9
ions awaiting human approval.\n- [Connect an MCP server](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-connections/connect-an-mcp-s
erver.md): Starts a connection request for an MCP server URL. Discovery, browser consent, and validation happen asynchronously; po
ll the returned `connectionRequestId` until the status is terminal. When the next step belongs to a person, the response carries a
`handoffUrl` to open.\n- [Get a connection request](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-connections/get-a-connection-req
uest.md): Current state of one connection request. Metered on its own poll budget rather than the shared per-caller one, so pollin
g on a short interval is expected and will not spend the budget your other calls need. A 429 here means the poll interval itself i
s too fast; honour Retry-After.\n- [Cancel a connection request](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-connections/cancel-a
-connection-request.md): Stops a request and invalidates its handoff link. Cancelling an already-terminal request is a no-op.\n- [
Retry validation](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-connections/retry-validation.md): Re-arms a stalled validation imme
diately instead of waiting out its backoff. Does not revive a terminal request — after `failed`, `expired`, or `cancelled`, start
a new one.\n- [List personas](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/list-personas.md): The project's personas, newest first
. Archived personas are excluded.\n- [Create a persona](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/create-a-persona.md): Creates
one persona. To draft several with a model first, use `POST /projects/{projectId}/personas/generate` — that route persists nothin
g.\n- [Get a persona](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/get-a-persona.md): A persona that lives in a DIFFERENT project
answers 404, never 403 — the route is not an existence oracle for a project you cannot see.\n- [Delete a persona](https://docs.mcp
jam.com/api-reference/swarms/delete-a-persona.md): Refused with 409 while goals still reference this persona — deleting it would s
trand them.\n- [Update a persona](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/update-a-persona.md): Partial update. Goals referen
ce the persona by id, so renaming one does not disturb anything pointing at it.\n- [Draft personas with a model](https://docs.mcpj
am.com/api-reference/swarms/draft-personas-with-a-model.md): Returns DRAFTS and persists nothing. That separation is deliberate: g
eneration is the step most likely to produce something nobody wanted, and a route that both invented and saved would make \"let me
see what you'd suggest\" indistinguishable from \"fill my project with these\".\n- [Draft journeys for a persona](https://docs.mc
pjam.com/api-reference/swarms/draft-journeys-for-a-persona.md): Returns DRAFTS and persists nothing — see `POST /projects/{project
Id}/personas/generate` for why, and for the quota this counts against.\n- [Get a journey](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/sw
arms/get-a-journey.md)\n- [Archive a journey](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/archive-a-journey.md): ARCHIVES rather
than deletes, and the response says so. Existing runs keep pointing at the definition they executed, so their history stays readab
le.\n- [Update a journey](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/update-a-journey.md): Editing a goal never disturbs a run a
lready under way: a run pins its own immutable snapshot of the definition at launch.\n- [List swarms](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-
reference/swarms/list-swarms.md)\n- [Create a swarm](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/create-a-swarm.md): A swarm is a
n authoring container holding DEFAULTS for the goals made under it. Creating one starts nothing.\n- [Get a swarm](https://docs.mcp
jam.com/api-reference/swarms/get-a-swarm.md)\n- [Archive a swarm](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/archive-a-swarm.md)
: ARCHIVES the container. The goals authored under it are not touched — they keep their own definitions and stay launchable.\n- [U
pdate a swarm](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/update-a-swarm.md): Changes the container's DEFAULTS. Goals already au
thored under it keep the values they were created with — this is not a cascade.\n- [List journeys](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-ref
erence/swarms/list-journeys.md): The project's goals, newest first. Archived goals are excluded.\n- [Create a journey](https://doc
s.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/create-a-journey.md): Creates one goal: a persona pursuing a task against one or more environmen
ts. To draft several with a model first, use `POST /projects/{projectId}/goals/generate` — that route persists nothing.\n- [List s
ecrets](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/secrets/list-secrets.md): The project's credentials as METADATA ONLY — no value is r
eturned by this or any other route. Shows the project-shared secrets plus the caller's own personal ones; another member's persona
l secret does not appear at all, not even its name.\n- [Create a secret](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/secrets/create-a-se
cret.md): Store a credential so environments can grant it to runs. THE VALUE TRAVELS IN THE REQUEST BODY and becomes visible to wh
atever makes the call. The response is metadata only. Creating a project-shared secret requires project admin; a personal one does
not.\n- [Get a secret](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/secrets/get-a-secret.md): One secret's metadata: delivery mode, host
binding, sharing, and when it was last handed to a run. Never its value. A secret from another project — and another member's per
sonal secret — both read as 404.\n- [Delete a secret](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/secrets/delete-a-secret.md): Delete a
stored credential. HARD — the row and the encrypted value both go, and MCPJam stops delivering it. Deliberately NOT blocked when a
n environment still selects it: refusing would leave a leaked credential undeletable until someone edited every environment naming
it, and deletion must never wa…\n- [Rotate or re-bind a secret](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/secrets/rotate-or-re-bind-a
-secret.md): Rotate the value and/or change how it is delivered. A rotation reaches NEW RUNS ONLY: a session already running holds
the old value — materialized in its box's environment, or inside an egress policy that cannot be read back — and there is no safe
way to replace it mid-run.\n- [List a journey's runs](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarm-runs/list-a-journeys-runs.md):
Newest first. Compact records — `attempts` is on the single-run read.\n- [Launch a journey](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/
swarm-runs/launch-a-journey.md): Answers **202**: the run row exists and its fan-out has started. It is not finished — poll `GET /
projects/{projectId}/goal-runs/{runId}` until `status` leaves `running`.\n- [Get a journey run](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-refere
nce/swarm-runs/get-a-journey-run.md): The full record, including per-session `attempts` and `targetSummaries`.\n- [List a run's se
ssions](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarm-runs/list-a-runs-sessions.md): One entry per chat session the run produced. Su
mmaries, not transcripts — read a transcript through the chat-session routes using `id`.\n- [Cancel a journey run](https://docs.mc
pjam.com/api-reference/swarm-runs/cancel-a-journey-run.md): Accepts a durable Stop request and returns immediately. cleanupPending
indicates that attempts are being settled in the background; status remains the current stored run status. IDEMPOTENT: cancelling
an already-cancelled run answers 200 with `alreadyCanceled: true` and `finalized: 0`, not a 409.\n- [Project swarm roll-up](https
://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarm-insights/project-swarm-roll-up.md): Recent runs with their goal-completion rates and repeat
-failure findings, plus a project-wide trend. Deterministic and free — start here.\n- [Get a run's rubric scorecard](https://docs.
mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarm-insights/get-a-runs-rubric-scorecard.md): The deterministic rubric result for one run. No model, no
spend.\n- [List swarm findings](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarm-insights/list-swarm-findings.md): Criteria that keep
failing, tracked across waves. One finding is one problem OVER TIME — `occurrenceCount` and `status` carry the history, so do not
treat repeat appearances as separate problems.\n- [Dismiss a finding](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarm-insights/dismiss
